title: Liver, biliary tree and pancreas

steps.tx: Under **LI-RADS** criteria, definitive **hepatocellular carcinoma** (LR-5) on multiphasic CT or MRI requires non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement in a lesion measuring 10 mm or greater. In addition, the lesion must demonstrate non-peripheral washout or threshold growth defined as a 50% or greater increase in diameter within 6 months, or an enhancing capsule when 20 mm or larger.
steps.say: Under LI-RADS criteria, definitive hepatocellular carcinoma, designated as LR-5, on multiphasic CT or MRI requires non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement in a lesion measuring 10 millimetres or greater. In addition, the lesion must demonstrate non-peripheral washout or threshold growth defined as a 50% or greater increase in diameter within 6 months, or an enhancing capsule when 20 millimetres or larger.

steps.tx: A **Hepatic haemangioma** typically appears as a well-circumscribed, T2 hyperintense lesion on MRI examinations. Dynamic contrast imaging exhibits peripheral nodular discontinuous arterial enhancement, followed by progressive **centripetal** fill-in on portal venous and delayed phases matching blood pool attenuation without abnormal early arteriovenous shunting.

rows: Early filling of peripheral vascular lakes
Uniform contrast pooling in sluggish cavernous spaces

steps.tx: **Focal nodular hyperplasia** demonstrates intense, homogeneous arterial enhancement with near-isointensity on portal venous phases. A pathognomonic central fibrous **stellate scar** exhibits delayed contrast enhancement on 10 to 20 minute delayed phases due to abundant myxoid stroma, differentiating it from hepatic adenomas.
steps.say: Focal nodular hyperplasia demonstrates intense, homogeneous arterial enhancement with near-isointensity on portal venous phases. A pathognomonic central fibrous stellate scar exhibits delayed contrast enhancement on 10 to 20 minute delayed phases due to abundant myxoid stroma, differentiating it from hepatic adenomas.

left.title: Focal Nodular Hyperplasia
points: Central stellate scar with delayed enhancement
Isointense to liver on portal venous phase
Contains functional hepatocytes and bile ducts

right.title: Hepatic Adenoma
points: Lack of bile ducts, fails to excrete Eovist
Bleeding and malignant risk in beta-catenin type

img.alt: Multiphasic MRI demonstrating central fibrous scar and intense arterial phase enhancement in FNH
img.caption: Arterial hyperenhancement and delayed central scar enhancement in FNH

steps.tx: **Budd-Chiari syndrome** results from acute or chronic hepatic venous outflow obstruction involving the major hepatic veins. Computed tomography demonstrates heterogeneous parenchymal perfusion with peripheral hypoperfusion and compensatory massive **caudate lobe** hypertrophy, which preserves independent venous drainage directly into the retrohepatic inferior vena cava.
steps.say: Budd-Chiari syndrome results from acute or chronic hepatic venous outflow obstruction involving the major hepatic veins. Computed tomography demonstrates heterogeneous parenchymal perfusion with peripheral hypoperfusion and compensatory massive caudate lobe hypertrophy, which preserves independent venous drainage directly into the retrohepatic inferior vena cava.

rows: Direct independent drainage into IVC spared from hepatic vein thrombosis
Elevated sinusoidal pressure and ischemic atrophy
Arterialization of caudate with delayed peripheral washout
Mass effect from massively hypertrophied caudate lobe

steps.tx: Perihilar **cholangiocarcinoma**, known as a **Klatskin tumour**, arises at the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts. Cross-sectional imaging demonstrates an infiltrating periductal soft tissue mass causing marked intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation with non-dilated extrahepatic ducts and hepatic capsular retraction.
steps.say: Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, known as a Klatskin tumour, arises at the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts. Cross-sectional imaging demonstrates an infiltrating periductal soft tissue mass causing marked intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation with non-dilated extrahepatic ducts and hepatic capsular retraction.

left.title: Klatskin Tumour Features
points: Infiltrative mass at hepatic duct bifurcation
Normal caliber non-dilated extrahepatic common duct
Delayed contrast enhancement from fibrous stroma
Frequent vascular encasement of portal vein

right.title: Bismuth-Corlette Staging
points: Type 1: Below confluence of common hepatic duct
Type 2: Reaching bifurcation without branch extension
Type 3: Extending into right (3a) or left (3b) hepatic duct
Type 4: Involving bilateral secondary intrahepatic branches

img.caption: Biliary ductal dilation and confluence infiltration in Klatskin cholangiocarcinoma

steps.tx: **Autoimmune pancreatitis** type 1 is a systemic manifestation of **IgG4**-related fibroinflammatory disease. Computed tomography classically displays diffuse, sausage-like pancreatic enlargement with loss of normal lobular architecture, a hypoattenuating capsule-like halo rim, and delayed parenchymal contrast enhancement without prominent acute peripancreatic fat stranding.
steps.say: Autoimmune pancreatitis type 1 is a systemic manifestation of IgG4-related fibroinflammatory disease. Computed tomography classically displays diffuse, sausage-like pancreatic enlargement with loss of normal lobular architecture, a hypoattenuating capsule-like halo rim, and delayed parenchymal contrast enhancement without prominent acute peripancreatic fat stranding.

rows: Loss of lobular clefts and contour definition
Dense fibroinflammatory rim with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
Fibrosis delaying contrast transit on late scans
Dramatic resolution following systemic corticosteroid therapy

steps.tx: **Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma** typically presents on dual-phase CT as an ill-defined, hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head. Obstruction triggers the pathognomonic **double-duct sign**, characterized by simultaneous dilation of the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct with abrupt transition.
steps.say: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma typically presents on dual-phase CT as an ill-defined, hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head. Obstruction triggers the pathognomonic double-duct sign, characterized by simultaneous dilation of the common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct with abrupt transition.

left.title: Double-Duct Sign
points: Dilation of common bile duct (> 8 mm)
Dilation of main pancreatic duct (> 3 mm)
Abrupt transition point in pancreatic head
High positive predictive value for malignancy

right.title: Vascular Infiltration Criteria
points: Coeliac axis and superior mesenteric artery involvement
Venous occlusion of superior mesenteric vein

steps.tx: **Mucinous cystic neoplasm** of the pancreas arises almost exclusively in women exceeding 95% of cases, located predominantly within the pancreatic body or tail. Cross-sectional imaging reveals a thick-walled multilocular macrocystic lesion with internal septations, containing pathognomonic **ovarian-type stroma** on histopathology.

rows: Women > 95%, body and tail of pancreas
Internal enhancing septa and peripheral calcification
High-grade dysplasia or invasive adenocarcinoma risk
